// Expected values for a busy road that drains (docs/rules/carriers.md, "A busy road" and "The carriers of a busy road"), captured from the
// original program in the emulator (ADR 0008): tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished mill (type 15) at a flag, as
// mill-walks.txt runs it, reduced to the passes that matter. The command lays one grain on the castle's flag at the pass 600 and four stones
// on the mill's flag at the pass 1400. The stones make the road from the mill's flag to the castle's busy, so a settler without a job of the
// castle (slot 2) becomes its second carrier beside the first (slot 5); once the stones and the flour are gone, the carrier of slot 2 turns
// at a flag with nothing to take four times, leaves the road at the pass 2674, and walks to the castle, whose door it reaches at the pass
// 2971. A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb command; each line after it gives, for a pass, the 16 bytes of the carriers
// (s2=, s5=) where they changed, the status byte and the six road bytes of the castle's flag (f1=, bytes 5 to 11) and of the mill's flag
// (f2=) where they changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they stand. The flags carry the original's numbers, from 1. Not production
// code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
